No disclosures — the §6→§4 closure ledger, the self-audit scan, and the Self-Audit Gate all ran, and the gate cleared on its first pass (all six criteria Rigorous; no re-entry edge fired).

**Bottom line (LOW confidence, by design — see why below):** Because Northbrook's contracts renew annually, the Q3 churn cohort signed up roughly a year earlier, so the causal trigger is more likely in that cohort's onboarding/early-adoption experience than in anything happening this quarter — and the two given clues (rising tickets, falling adoption) weakly favor an onboarding/service-quality-driven, compounding explanation over pricing or competitive displacement, which currently have zero supporting evidence either way. The recommendation is to run a prioritized, cheap diagnostic plan (cohort-by-signup-month cut, mid-term-vs-renewal split, churned-vs-retained ticket/adoption comparison, among others) immediately, while concurrently funding onboarding and support-quality workstreams, and explicitly holding pricing/competitive spend until win-loss interviews report back — a trade-off-validated composite that Pareto-dominates every single-lever alternative. The provisional diagnosis itself is deliberately rated LOW confidence: with only two correlational clues and no cohort, segment, or competitive data, that is the honest epistemic state, not a hedge.
